third_party_evaluations.summary: Rapid evidence acquisition from diverse devices in time-critical settings.

evaluation.rationale: Independent reviews of the stored evidence produced specialty: 3. The existing unordered-specialty rule applies when at least one reviewer identifies a specialty track. See each persona rationale for the supporting factors and limitations.

hiroshi-tanaka.rationale: Time-critical evidence acquisition across devices is a focused forensic specialization, backed by recorded accreditation; neither cost nor training recognition establishes broader incident-command seniority.

maria-okonkwo.rationale: Time-critical evidence acquisition across devices is a focused forensic specialty with recorded accreditation and COOL recognition. The narrow use case and absence of detailed practical logistics prevent treating it as general incident-response seniority.

alex-novak.rationale: Rapid evidence acquisition across devices under time pressure is a distinct forensic use case. The recorded specialty hint and explicitly narrow scope fit this classification without inferring a broad expert level.
